evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2C.

claim: Ded1 NTD residues 83–89 appear to be most important for binding to GST-eIF4E.
source: Using the same GST pull-down assay as above, we observed that substituting Ded1 NTD residues 21–27, 29–35 and 51–57 conferred the greatest reductions in binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B, cols. 5, 6, 8, bars in green hues), whereas residues 59–65 and 83–89 appear to be most important for binding to GST-eIF4E (Figure 2C, cols. 9,11, orange hues).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2C.

claim: The critical binding determinants for eIF4A map between residues 21–57 of the Ded1 NTD.
source: These findings suggested that the critical binding determinants for eIF4A and eIF4E are located in adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the Ded1 NTD, located within residues 21–57 for eIF4A and within residues 59–89 for eIF4E.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2B.

claim: The critical binding determinants for eIF4E map between residues 59–89 of the Ded1 NTD.
source: These findings suggested that the critical binding determinants for eIF4A and eIF4E are located in adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the Ded1 NTD, located within residues 21–57 for eIF4A and within residues 59–89 for eIF4E.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2C.

claim: Combining the contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 29–35 produced no further reduction in binding to GST-eIF4A compared to the single substitutions.
source: Whereas combining the contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 29–35 produced no further reduction in binding to GST-eIF4A compared to the single substitutions (Figure 2B, cols. 13 vs. 5 and 6), an additive reduction in binding was observed on combining the non-contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 51–57 (Figure 2B, cols. 14 vs. 5 and eight and Figure 2—figure supplement 2, cols. 5 vs. 1 and 2), which was comparable in its effect to deleting the entire (ΔNTD2-92) on binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B, cols. 2 and 14, dark green hues).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: An additive reduction in binding to GST-eIF4A was observed on combining the non-contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 51–57.
source: Whereas combining the contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 29–35 produced no further reduction in binding to GST-eIF4A compared to the single substitutions (Figure 2B, cols. 13 vs. 5 and 6), an additive reduction in binding was observed on combining the non-contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 51–57 (Figure 2B, cols. 14 vs. 5 and eight and Figure 2—figure supplement 2, cols. 5 vs. 1 and 2), which was comparable in its effect to deleting the entire (ΔNTD2-92) on binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B, cols. 2 and 14, dark green hues).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 21-27/51-57 double substitution was comparable in its effect to deleting the entire NTD (ΔNTD2-92) on binding to GST-eIF4A.
source: Whereas combining the contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 29–35 produced no further reduction in binding to GST-eIF4A compared to the single substitutions (Figure 2B, cols. 13 vs. 5 and 6), an additive reduction in binding was observed on combining the non-contiguous substitutions 21–27 and 51–57 (Figure 2B, cols. 14 vs. 5 and eight and Figure 2—figure supplement 2, cols. 5 vs. 1 and 2), which was comparable in its effect to deleting the entire (ΔNTD2-92) on binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B, cols. 2 and 14, dark green hues).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: Combining the non-contiguous substitutions 59-65 and 83-89 that individually impaired eIF4E binding produced reductions in binding by the 59-65/83-89 variant indistinguishable from those generated by the single substitutions.
source: In contrast, combining the non-contiguous substitutions that individually impaired eIF4E binding produced reductions in binding by the 59-65/83-89 variant indistinguishable from those generated by the single substitutions (Figure 2C, cols. 16 vs. 9 and 11 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2, cols. 12 vs. 9 and 10).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The two double substitutions that impair binding to GST-eIF4A (21-27/29-35 and 21-27/51-57) had little or no effect on binding to GST-eIF4E.
source: It is noteworthy that the two double substitutions that impair binding to GST-eIF4A (21-27/29-35 and 21-27/51-57) had little or no effect on binding to GST-eIF4E (Figure 2B–C, cols. 13–14), and that the double substitution 59-65/83-89 strongly reduced binding to GST-eIF4E with no significant effect on binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B–C, col. 16).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: The double substitution 59-65/83-89 strongly reduced binding to GST-eIF4E with no significant effect on binding to GST-eIF4A.
source: It is noteworthy that the two double substitutions that impair binding to GST-eIF4A (21-27/29-35 and 21-27/51-57) had little or no effect on binding to GST-eIF4E (Figure 2B–C, cols. 13–14), and that the double substitution 59-65/83-89 strongly reduced binding to GST-eIF4E with no significant effect on binding to GST-eIF4A (Figure 2B–C, col. 16).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: The binding determinants for eIF4A and eIF4E are segregated into non-overlapping adjacent segments of the NTD.
source: These last findings support the notion that the binding determinants for eIF4A and eIF4E are segregated into non-overlapping adjacent segments of the NTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Combining substitution 51–57 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4A with the adjacent substitution 59–65 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4E produced a binding defect to GST-eIF4E indistinguishable from that given by 59–65 alone.
source: Combining substitution 51–57 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4A with the adjacent substitution 59–65 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4E produced a binding defect to GST-eIF4E indistinguishable from that given by 59–65 alone (Figure 2C, cols. 15 vs. 8 and 9), supporting our conclusion that the binding determinants for eIF4E do not extend upstream into the region that binds eIF4A.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2C.

claim: The binding determinants for eIF4E do not extend upstream into the region that binds eIF4A.
source: Combining substitution 51–57 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4A with the adjacent substitution 59–65 that selectively impairs binding to GST-eIF4E produced a binding defect to GST-eIF4E indistinguishable from that given by 59–65 alone (Figure 2C, cols. 15 vs. 8 and 9), supporting our conclusion that the binding determinants for eIF4E do not extend upstream into the region that binds eIF4A.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2C.

claim: The 59–65 substitution appeared to suppress the eIF4A binding defect of the adjacent upstream substitution 51–57 in the 51-57/59-65 variant.
source: However, the 59–65 substitution appeared to suppress the eIF4A binding defect of the adjacent upstream substitution 51–57 in the 51-57/59-65 variant (Figure 2B, cols. 15 vs. 8 and 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: The residues in segment 59–65 that mediate eIF4E binding also antagonize binding of eIF4A to the contiguous segment 51–57 segment.
source: One way to explain this 'context dependence' of the 51–57 substitution would be to propose that the residues in segment 59–65 that mediate eIF4E binding also antagonize binding of eIF4A to the contiguous segment 51–57 segment, such that their removal lessens the requirement for the eIF4A binding determinants in the 51–57 segment.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation proposed to account for the data in Figure 2B.

claim: The 59–65 substitution did not suppress the stronger binding defect conferred by combining the non-contiguous substitution 21–27 with 51–57 in a 21-27/51-57/59-65 triple mutant.
source: Consistent with this possibility, we found that the 59–65 substitution did not suppress the stronger binding defect conferred by combining the non-contiguous substitution 21–27 with 51–57 in a 21-27/51-57/59-65 triple mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, col. eight vs. col. 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double substitutions provide Ded1 variants that selectively impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E for in vivo analysis.
source: Regardless of the explanation, the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double substitutions provide Ded1 variants that selectively impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E for our subsequent in vivo analysis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: R27A impaired binding to GST-eIF4A to the same extent observed on substituting the entire cluster 21–27 in which R27 resides.
source: Interestingly, R27A impaired binding to GST-eIF4A to the same extent observed on substituting the entire cluster 21–27 in which R27 resides, whereas G28A and R51A had no effect (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: G28A and R51A had no effect on binding to GST-eIF4A.
source: Interestingly, R27A impaired binding to GST-eIF4A to the same extent observed on substituting the entire cluster 21–27 in which R27 resides, whereas G28A and R51A had no effect (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: R27 is highly conserved in the family Saccharomycetaceae, as well as in animals.
source: This finding is in accordance with the fact that R27 is highly conserved in the family Saccharomycetaceae, as well as in animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B), whereas, G28 and R51 are not.
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by the sequence alignments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: G28 and R51 are not highly conserved.
source: This finding is in accordance with the fact that R27 is highly conserved in the family Saccharomycetaceae, as well as in animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B), whereas, G28 and R51 are not.
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by the sequence alignments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Ala substitution of R62 within the region implicated in eIF4E binding had no significant effect on binding to GST-eIF4E.
source: In contrast, despite its strong sequence conservation, Ala substitution of R62 within the region implicated in eIF4E binding had no significant effect on binding to GST-eIF4E (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B, right graph); although we note that the adjacent residue at position 61 is also an Arg in S. cerevisiae.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Substituting each of the aromatic residues Y65 and W88 reduced binding to GST-eIF4E to the same extent observed for Ala substitutions of the entire corresponding segments 59–65 and 83–89, respectively.
source: Strikingly, substituting each of the aromatic residues Y65 and W88 reduced binding to GST-eIF4E to the same extent observed for Ala substitutions of the entire corresponding segments 59–65 and 83–89, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the GST pull-down assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Aromatic residues Y65 and W88 within segments 59–65 and 83–89 might mediate key hydrophobic interactions with eIF4E.
source: Together, these last findings reinforce the identification of segments 59–65 and 83–89 as binding determinants for eIF4E, and further suggest that aromatic residues Y65 and W88 within these segments might mediate key hydrophobic interactions with eIF4E.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C.

claim: W88 is invariant among the eukaryotic species examined.
source: Although Y65 is not highly conserved, W88 is invariant among the eukaryotic species we examined (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by the sequence alignments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Y65 is not highly conserved.
source: Although Y65 is not highly conserved, W88 is invariant among the eukaryotic species we examined (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by the sequence alignments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: The ded1-ts alleles also containing the 21–27 or 51–57 mutations shown above to impair eIF4A binding in vitro conferred stronger Slg- phenotypes at 34°C compared to ded1-ts alone.
source: Compared to ded1-ts alone, the ded1-ts alleles also containing the 21–27 or 51–57 mutations shown above to impair eIF4A binding in vitro conferred stronger Slg- phenotypes at 34°C, with a slightly greater defect when the two mutations were combined within ded1-ts-21-27/51-57 (Figure 3B, 34°C, rows 6–9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 59–65, 83–89, and 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair eIF4E binding to Ded1 in vitro conferred Slg- phenotypes in combination with ded1-ts.
source: Similar findings were made for the 59–65, 83–89, and 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair eIF4E binding to Ded1 in vitro (Figure 3B, row 6 vs. 10–12), except that the reductions in growth were less pronounced than observed for the 21–27 and 21-27/51-57 mutations that impair eIF4A binding (Figure 3B, cf. rows 10–12 vs. 7 and 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The reductions in growth conferred by the 59–65, 83–89, and 59-65/83-89 mutations were less pronounced than observed for the 21–27 and 21-27/51-57 mutations that impair eIF4A binding.
source: Similar findings were made for the 59–65, 83–89, and 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair eIF4E binding to Ded1 in vitro (Figure 3B, row 6 vs. 10–12), except that the reductions in growth were less pronounced than observed for the 21–27 and 21-27/51-57 mutations that impair eIF4A binding (Figure 3B, cf. rows 10–12 vs. 7 and 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 14–20 and Δ40–47 mutations that did not affect Ded1 binding to eIF4A or eIF4E in vitro also conferred no Slg- in combination with ded1-ts in vivo.
source: In contrast, the 14–20 and Δ40–47 mutations that did not affect Ded1 binding to eIF4A or eIF4E in vitro also conferred no Slg- in combination with ded1-ts in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Neither the double substitution 21-27/51-57 nor the quadruple substitution 21-27/51-57,59-65/83-89 reduced the steady-state level of the ded1-ts product.
source: Western analysis showed that neither the double substitution 21-27/51-57 nor the quadruple substitution 21-27/51-57,59-65/83-89 reduced the steady-state level of the ded1-ts product (Figure 3D, lanes 5–7), indicating that they impair Ded1 function and not its expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the Western blot shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The NTD substitutions impair Ded1 function and not its expression.
source: Western analysis showed that neither the double substitution 21-27/51-57 nor the quadruple substitution 21-27/51-57,59-65/83-89 reduced the steady-state level of the ded1-ts product (Figure 3D, lanes 5–7), indicating that they impair Ded1 function and not its expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Western blot data in Figure 3D.

claim: The single amino acid substitutions Y21A and R27A in the eIF4A binding region each conferred a Slg- phenotype at 34°C in combination with ded1-ts.
source: The single amino acid substitutions Y21A and R27A in the eIF4A binding region each conferred a Slg- phenotype at 34°C in combination with ded1-ts, which for R27A was greater than that observed for Y21A and comparable to that given by the 21–27 clustered substitution that encompasses both single-residue substitutions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, rows 5–6 vs. 2–3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Slg- phenotype conferred by R27A was greater than that observed for Y21A and comparable to that given by the 21–27 clustered substitution.
source: The single amino acid substitutions Y21A and R27A in the eIF4A binding region each conferred a Slg- phenotype at 34°C in combination with ded1-ts, which for R27A was greater than that observed for Y21A and comparable to that given by the 21–27 clustered substitution that encompasses both single-residue substitutions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, rows 5–6 vs. 2–3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: These phenotypes correlate with the stronger eIF4A binding defect given by R27A versus Y21A, and with the similar binding defects observed for R27A and the 21–27 variant in vitro.
source: These phenotypes correlate with the stronger eIF4A binding defect given by R27A versus Y21A, and with the similar binding defects observed for R27A and the 21–27 variant in vitro (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the growth data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 with the binding data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The F56A/F57A substitutions in the 51–57 interval had no effect on cell growth in combination with ded1-ts.
source: The F56A/F57A substitutions in the 51–57 interval, which had no effect on GST-eIF4A binding in vitro (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B) also had no effect on cell growth in combination with ded1-ts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, rows 2 and 7).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Y65A and W88A single residue substitutions in the respective 59–65 and 83–89 segments of the eIF4E binding region each conferred moderate Slg- phenotypes in combination with ded1-ts indistinguishable from those given by the corresponding 59–65 and 83–89 clustered substitutions.
source: The Y65A and W88A single residue substitutions in the respective 59–65 and 83–89 segments of the eIF4E binding region each conferred moderate Slg- phenotypes in combination with ded1-ts indistinguishable from those given by the corresponding 59–65 and 83–89 clustered substitutions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, rows 11–12 vs. 9–10).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The effects of single-residue and clustered NTD substitutions on Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A or GST-eIF4E in vitro are generally well correlated with their effects on cell growth in combination with the ded1-ts allele.
source: Taken together, the effects of single-residue and clustered NTD substitutions on Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A or GST-eIF4E in vitro are generally well correlated with their effects on cell growth in combination with the ded1-ts allele, with relatively stronger growth defects associated with mutations that reduce Ded1 binding to eIF4A versus those conferring comparable reductions in Ded1 binding to eIF4E.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the binding data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4 with the growth data in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Relatively stronger growth defects are associated with mutations that reduce Ded1 binding to eIF4A versus those conferring comparable reductions in Ded1 binding to eIF4E.
source: Taken together, the effects of single-residue and clustered NTD substitutions on Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A or GST-eIF4E in vitro are generally well correlated with their effects on cell growth in combination with the ded1-ts allele, with relatively stronger growth defects associated with mutations that reduce Ded1 binding to eIF4A versus those conferring comparable reductions in Ded1 binding to eIF4E.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the binding data in Figure 2 with the growth data in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 21-27/51-57 double cluster mutation affecting eIF4A binding confers a cold-sensitive Slg- phenotype.
source: We also examined the effects of the NTD mutations on Ded1 function in the absence of the ded1-ts mutation, finding that the 21-27/51-57 double cluster mutation affecting eIF4A binding confers a cold-sensitive Slg- phenotype, which is exacerbated on combining it with the 59-65/83-89 double cluster mutations that impair eIF4E binding in vitro (Figure 3C, rows 1–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The cold-sensitive Slg- phenotype of 21-27/51-57 is exacerbated on combining it with the 59-65/83-89 double cluster mutations that impair eIF4E binding in vitro.
source: We also examined the effects of the NTD mutations on Ded1 function in the absence of the ded1-ts mutation, finding that the 21-27/51-57 double cluster mutation affecting eIF4A binding confers a cold-sensitive Slg- phenotype, which is exacerbated on combining it with the 59-65/83-89 double cluster mutations that impair eIF4E binding in vitro (Figure 3C, rows 1–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The quadruple mutation 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 conferred a strong Slg- phenotype comparable to that given by the ded1-Δ2–90 deletion allele lacking nearly the entire NTD.
source: Interestingly, the latter quadruple mutation conferred a strong Slg- phenotype comparable to that given by the ded1-Δ2–90 deletion allele lacking nearly the entire NTD, both in otherwise WT DED1 (Figure 3C, rows 4–5) and in the ded1-ts allele, which suggests that binding to eIF4A and eIF4E constitutes the key in vivo function of the Ded1 NTD.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Binding to eIF4A and eIF4E constitutes the key in vivo function of the Ded1 NTD.
source: Interestingly, the latter quadruple mutation conferred a strong Slg- phenotype comparable to that given by the ded1-Δ2–90 deletion allele lacking nearly the entire NTD, both in otherwise WT DED1 (Figure 3C, rows 4–5) and in the ded1-ts allele, which suggests that binding to eIF4A and eIF4E constitutes the key in vivo function of the Ded1 NTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 3C.

claim: The double and quadruple substitutions, as well as the Δ2–90 NTD deletion, had little effect on Ded1 steady-state expression levels.
source: Again, Western analysis revealed that the double and quadruple substitutions, as well as the Δ2–90 NTD deletion, had little effect on Ded1 steady-state expression levels (Figure 3D, lanes 1–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the Western blot shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The CTD deletion that removes the C-terminal 43 residues of Ded1 (ded1-ΔC) confers no growth defect when the rest of Ded1 is intact.
source: Consistent with previous findings (Hilliker et al., 2011), the CTD deletion that removes the C-terminal 43 residues of Ded1 (ded1-ΔC) confers no growth defect when the rest of Ded1 is intact.
evidence: This is stated as a finding consistent with prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The ΔC mutation exacerbates the cold-sensitive Slg- phenotypes of all of the ded1 mutations examined containing single- or double cluster substitutions in the NTD that impair binding to either eIF4A or eIF4E.
source: Importantly, however, the ΔC mutation exacerbates the cold-sensitive Slg- phenotypes of all of the ded1 mutations examined containing single- or double cluster substitutions in the NTD that impair binding to either eIF4A or eIF4E.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The exacerbation by ΔC is subtle for the 51–57, 59–65, and 83–89 single-cluster mutations, but is pronounced for 21–27 and both double-cluster substitutions.
source: While the exacerbation by ΔC is subtle for the 51–57, 59–65, and 83–89 single-cluster mutations, it is pronounced for 21–27 and both double-cluster substitutions (Figure 4A, cf. adjacent rows).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The exacerbation of the cold-sensitive growth phenotype of the NTD double-cluster mutations by ΔC occurred without reducing expression relative to the NTD variants with an intact CTD.
source: The exacerbation of the cold-sensitive growth phenotype of the NTD double-cluster mutations by ΔC occurred without reducing expression relative to the NTD variants with an intact CTD (Figure 4B, lanes 4–6).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the Western blot shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Interaction of the Ded1 CTD with eIF4G is less critical for stabilizing the Ded1-eIF4E-eIF4A-eIF4G quaternary complex, activating Ded1 helicase function, or both, compared to the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A.
source: These findings are consistent with the idea that interaction of the Ded1 CTD with eIF4G is less critical for stabilizing the Ded1-eIF4E-eIF4A-eIF4G quaternary complex, activating Ded1 helicase function, or both, compared to the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A; but that the importance of the CTD is increased when either the Ded1-eIF4E or Ded1-eIF4A interactions are impaired.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 4A.

claim: The importance of the Ded1 CTD is increased when either the Ded1-eIF4E or Ded1-eIF4A interactions are impaired.
source: These findings are consistent with the idea that interaction of the Ded1 CTD with eIF4G is less critical for stabilizing the Ded1-eIF4E-eIF4A-eIF4G quaternary complex, activating Ded1 helicase function, or both, compared to the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A; but that the importance of the CTD is increased when either the Ded1-eIF4E or Ded1-eIF4A interactions are impaired.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 4A.

claim: The eIF4A, eIF4E, and eIF4G1-HA all coimmunoprecipitated specifically with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts product.
source: The eIF4A, eIF4E, and eIF4G1-HA all coimmunoprecipitated specifically with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts product, failing to be immunoprecipitated from the extract lacking a myc-tagged protein (Figure 5, rows 5–6), as expected for Ded1 interaction with eIF4F.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claim: The presence of mutations 21-27/51-57 in the ded1-ts allele reduced coimmunoprecipitation of the myc13-tagged product with native eIF4A, but not eIF4E or eIF4G1-HA from WCEs.
source: The presence of mutations 21-27/51-57 in the ded1-ts allele, which impair Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A in vitro (Figure 2B) reduced coimmunoprecipitation of the myc13-tagged product with native eIF4A, but not eIF4E or eIF4G1-HA from WCEs (Figure 5, rows 6–7).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claim: Mutations 59-65/83-89 specifically impaired coimmunoprecipition of eIF4E with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 product.
source: Moreover, mutations 59-65/83-89, which reduced Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4E in vitro (Figure 2C), specifically impaired coimmunoprecipition of eIF4E with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 product (Figure 5, lanes 6 and 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claim: The coimmunoprecipitation results were unaffected by treating the immune complexes with RNAses A and T1, suggesting that the interactions are not bridged by RNA.
source: The results were unaffected by treating the immune complexes with RNAses A and T1 (Figure 5, lanes 9–12 vs. 5–8), suggesting that the interactions are not bridged by RNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claim: The binding determinants in the Ded1 NTD for eIF4A and eIF4E defined by in vitro pull-down assays with recombinant GST fusions to eIF4A or eIF4E are also crucial for association of native eIF4A or eIF4E with the ded1-ts product expressed at native levels in yeast cells.
source: Thus, the binding determinants in the Ded1 NTD for eIF4A and eIF4E defined by in vitro pull-down assays with recombinant GST fusions to eIF4A or eIF4E are also crucial for association of native eIF4A or eIF4E with the ded1-ts product expressed at native levels in yeast cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the coimmunoprecipitation data in Figure 5.

claim: eIF4A overexpression mitigated the Slg- phenotypes at 34°C of the 21–27, 29–35, and 51–57 single-cluster mutations, and also the 21-27/29-35 double cluster mutations.
source: eIF4A overexpression mitigated the Slg- phenotypes at 34°C of the 21–27, 29–35, and 51–57 single-cluster mutations, and also the 21-27/29-35 double cluster mutations (Figure 6B, rows 3–10, cf. adjacent rows), all of which conferred partial reductions in Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A in vitro (Figure 2B), consistent with restored interaction of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6B.

claim: eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the stronger Slg- phenotype conferred by the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 double-cluster mutation.
source: Importantly however, eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the stronger Slg- phenotype conferred by the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 double-cluster mutation (Figure 6B, rows 11–12), which reduced binding to GST-eIF4A to the low level conferred by the ΔN2-92 deletion that removes the entire eIF4A binding domain (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6B.

claim: eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E.
source: Nor did eIF4A overexpression mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), supporting the interpretation that suppression of the other NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Suppression of the NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding by eIF4A overexpression results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action.
source: Nor did eIF4A overexpression mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), supporting the interpretation that suppression of the other NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ded1 substitutions in the eIF4A-binding region of the NTD confer growth defects in vivo owing to impaired association with eIF4A in cells.
source: These findings support the idea that Ded1 substitutions in the eIF4A-binding region of the NTD confer growth defects in vivo owing to impaired association with eIF4A in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpressing WT DED1 or the ded1-21-27/51-57 allele defective for eIF4A binding from a hc plasmid increased the growth rate of cdc33-1 cells.
source: In agreement with this, we found that overexpressing either WT DED1 or the ded1-21-27/51-57 allele defective for eIF4A binding from a hc plasmid increased the growth rate of cdc33-1 cells (Figure 7A, rows 3–4 vs. 1.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The hc ded1-59-65/83-89 allele, defective for eIF4E binding in vitro, had no effect on growth of the cdc33-1 mutant cells.
source: Importantly, however, the hc ded1-59-65/83-89 allele, defective for eIF4E binding in vitro, had no effect on growth of the mutant cells (Figure 7A, row 5 vs. 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The ded1-59-65/83-89 mutation impairs both a physical and functional interaction between Ded1 and eIF4E in cells.
source: These findings have two important implications. First, they provide strong evidence that the ded1-59-65/83-89 mutation impairs both a physical and functional interaction between Ded1 and eIF4E in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 7A.

claim: Overexpressing Ded1 partially suppresses the cdc33-1 mutation by enhancing interaction of the cdc33-1 product with Ded1 by mass action, presumably increasing the concentration of the eIF4F·Ded1 complex in which Ded1 functions most efficiently.
source: Second, they imply that overexpressing Ded1 partially suppresses the cdc33-1 mutation by enhancing interaction of the cdc33-1 product with Ded1 by mass action, presumably increasing the concentration of the eIF4F·Ded1 complex in which Ded1 functions most efficiently, rather than indirectly compensating for a reduction in eIF4F function (that should occur for all ded1 alleles).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 7A.

claim: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation.
source: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation, which was not significantly greater for one mutation versus the other (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The reduction in P/M ratio conferred by ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 was not significantly greater than that conferred by ded1-ts,59-65/83-89.
source: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation, which was not significantly greater for one mutation versus the other (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Introducing single- or double-cluster NTD mutations that impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E, or control NTD mutations 14–20 and 40–47 with no effect on eIF4A/eIF4E binding, had little or no effect on expression of the reporter lacking a 5'UTR SL.
source: Relative to the ded1-ts parental mutant, introducing single- or double-cluster NTD mutations that impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E, or control NTD mutations 14–20 and 40–47 with no effect on eIF4A/eIF4E binding, had little or no effect on expression of the reporter lacking a 5'UTR SL (Figure 8C, dark gray bars).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain.
source: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, cols. 1–2), which was unaffected by the control NTD mutations; but was driven even lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 that eliminate, respectively, eIF4A or eIF4E binding to Ded1 (Figure 8C, light gray bars).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of the cap-distal SL reporter was driven lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89.
source: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, cols. 1–2), which was unaffected by the control NTD mutations; but was driven even lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 that eliminate, respectively, eIF4A or eIF4E binding to Ded1 (Figure 8C, light gray bars).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain.
source: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was also reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, col. 3 vs. 1), and was not further diminished by the control NTD mutations or the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4E binding (59–65 and 83–89), whereas the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of this reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants (Figure 8C, white bars).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants.
source: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was also reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, col. 3 vs. 1), and was not further diminished by the control NTD mutations or the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4E binding (59–65 and 83–89), whereas the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of this reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants (Figure 8C, white bars).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Overexpression of eIF4A conferred increased expression of the no SL and cap-distal reporters in the ded1-ts/21–27 mutant, predicted to exhibit partially impaired binding of eIF4A to Ded1, but not in the ded1-ts/21-27/51-57 or ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 strains.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of eIF4A conferred increased expression of the no SL and cap-distal reporters in the ded1-ts/21–27 mutant, predicted to exhibit partially impaired binding of eIF4A to Ded1, but not in the ded1-ts/21-27/51-57 or ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 strains expected to be fully defective for eIF4A binding, or for eIF4E binding, respectively (Figure 8—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 5.

claim: The defect in reporter expression conferred by ded1-ts/21–27 involved impaired Ded1 association with eIF4A.
source: This supports the notion that the defect in reporter expression conferred by ded1-ts/21–27 involved impaired Ded1 association with eIF4A.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the luciferase assay data in Figure 8—figure supplement 5.

claim: In the eIF4E-binding mutant ded1-ts,59-65/83-89, the proportion of reporter mRNA in the heavy polysome fractions is reduced, and the proportion in the smallest polysomes and monosomes is increased relative to the mRNA distribution in the parental strain.
source: In the eIF4E-binding mutant ded1-ts,59-65/83-89, the proportion of reporter mRNA in the heavy polysome fractions is reduced, and the proportion in the smallest polysomes and monosomes is increased (Figure 8D (ii), orange points) relative to the mRNA distribution in the parental strain (Figure 8D (ii), grey points).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: In the eIF4A binding mutant ded1-ts,21-27/51-57, the proportion of reporter mRNA in heavy polysomes is reduced and the proportion in free mRNP is elevated compared to that seen in the ded1-ts strain.
source: Moreover, in the eIF4A binding mutant ded1-ts,21-27/51-57, the proportion of reporter mRNA in heavy polysomes is reduced and the proportion in free mRNP is elevated (Figure 8D (ii), green points) compared to that seen in the ded1-ts strain (Figure 8D (ii), grey points).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The more extensive shift from polysomes to free mRNP observed for the eIF4A-binding mutant compared to the shift from larger to smaller polysomes/monosomes conferred by the eIF4E-binding mutant is consistent with the relatively greater reductions in cap-proximal SL reporter expression given by the set of three eIF4A-binding mutants versus the three eIF4E-binding mutants.
source: The more extensive shift from polysomes to free mRNP observed for the eIF4A-binding mutant compared to the shift from larger to smaller polysomes/monosomes conferred by the eIF4E-binding mutant (Figure 8D (ii), green vs. orange) is consistent with the relatively greater reductions in cap-proximal SL reporter expression given by the set of three eIF4A-binding mutants versus the three eIF4E-binding mutants (Figure 8C, eIF4A(-) vs. eIF4E(-) mutants).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the polysome distribution data in Figure 8D with the luciferase assay data in Figure 8C.

claim: The polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations.
source: In contrast to the behavior of the reporter mRNA, the polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations (Figure 8D (i)), suggesting that Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
source: In contrast to the behavior of the reporter mRNA, the polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations (Figure 8D (i)), suggesting that Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the polysome distribution data in Figure 8D.

claim: ACT1 mRNA was not found to be hyperdependent on Ded1 by ribosome profiling of a ded1 mutant.
source: ACT1 mRNA was not found to be hyperdependent on Ded1 by ribosome profiling of a ded1 mutant (Sen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a fact from prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Loss of eIF4A and eIF4E interactions by the Ded1 NTD lead to reduced translation initiation of a Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNA, as well as to decreased bulk translation initiation in vivo.
source: These results confirm that loss of eIF4A and eIF4E interactions by the Ded1 NTD lead to reduced translation initiation of a Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNA, as well as to decreased bulk translation initiation in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the polysome profiling and luciferase assay data in Figure 8.

claim: The single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), compared to the parental ded1-ts strain.
source: Assaying expression of the same LUC reporters, we found that the single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), and that the Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), thus supporting the importance of these individual residues in Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain.
source: Assaying expression of the same LUC reporters, we found that the single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), and that the Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), thus supporting the importance of these individual residues in Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly.
source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2, the 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly (panel A) and expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters (panel B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters.
source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2, the 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly (panel A) and expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters (panel B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Eliminating both eIF4A and eIF4E binding simultaneously essentially inactivates the Ded1 NTD in promoting bulk translation as well as translation of Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNAs.
source: We also provided evidence that eliminating both eIF4A and eIF4E binding simultaneously essentially inactivates the Ded1 NTD in promoting bulk translation as well as translation of Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ded1-ΔC mutation has little or no effect on polysome assembly on its own.
source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A, the ded1-ΔC mutation analyzed above has little or no effect on polysome assembly on its own (cf. panels (i)-(ii)).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A.

claim: ΔC clearly exacerbates the effects of both the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double-cluster mutations in the Ded1 NTD in reducing P/M ratios, with a relatively greater effect for the 21-27/51-57 mutation that eliminates eIF4A binding.
source: However, ΔC clearly exacerbates the effects of both the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double-cluster mutations in the Ded1 NTD in reducing P/M ratios, with a relatively greater effect for the 21-27/51-57 mutation that eliminates eIF4A binding (cf. (iii)-(iv) and (v)-(vi)).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A.

claim: ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters.
source: Similarly, ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters, but ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set four vs. sets 2 and 3) and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set six vs. sets 2 and 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claim: ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation.
source: Similarly, ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters, but ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set four vs. sets 2 and 3) and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set six vs. sets 2 and 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Eliminating eIF4G association with the Ded1 CTD imposes a relatively greater requirement for the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E, either in forming or stabilizing the eIF4F·Ded1 complex or in stimulating Ded1 unwinding activity.
source: These findings support our conclusion that eliminating eIF4G association with the Ded1 CTD imposes a relatively greater requirement for the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E, either in forming or stabilizing the eIF4F·Ded1 complex or in stimulating Ded1 unwinding activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1.
source: In agreement with previous results (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1, and deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% (Figure 9A, cols. 1–3; see Figure 9—figure supplement 1C for data summary).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% on CP-8.1 mRNA.
source: In agreement with previous results (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1, and deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% (Figure 9A, cols. 1–3; see Figure 9—figure supplement 1C for data summary).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax on CP-8.1 mRNA.
source: Interestingly, disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax, whereas the 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax (Figure 9A, cols. 3–5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax on CP-8.1 mRNA.
source: Interestingly, disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax, whereas the 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax (Figure 9A, cols. 3–5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The ΔNTD1-116 truncation greatly increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on CP-8.1 mRNA.
source: The ΔNTD1-116 truncation also greatly increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on this mRNA (Figure 9B, cols. 1–2), as observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018); and both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions also increased the K1/2 for Ded1 to an extent ≈40% of that given by the ΔNTD1-116 (Figure 9B, cols. 2–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on CP-8.1 mRNA to an extent ≈40% of that given by the ΔNTD1-116.
source: The ΔNTD1-116 truncation also greatly increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on this mRNA (Figure 9B, cols. 1–2), as observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018); and both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions also increased the K1/2 for Ded1 to an extent ≈40% of that given by the ΔNTD1-116 (Figure 9B, cols. 2–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9B.

claim: FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold.
source: As observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold, and eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair this stimulation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 2–3); however, ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 2–3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair the stimulation of kmax on RPL41A mRNA.
source: As observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold, and eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair this stimulation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 2–3); however, ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 2–3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold.
source: As observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold, and eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair this stimulation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 2–3); however, ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 2–3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neither the 21-27/51-57 double substitution nor the 59–65 substitution altered the increase in kmax for RPL41A mRNA conferred by FL Ded1.
source: As expected, neither the 21-27/51-57 double substitution nor the 59–65 substitution altered the increase in kmax for RPL41A mRNA conferred by FL Ded1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 4–5 vs. 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA (~7 fold for 21-27/51-57 and ~4 fold for the 59–65 substitution), but these increases were much smaller than the ~70 fold increase produced by ΔNTD1-116.
source: While both substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 compared to FL-Ded1 (~7 fold for 21-27/51-57 and ~4 fold for the 59–65 substitution), these increases were much smaller than the ~70 fold increase produced by ΔNTD1-116 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 3–4 vs. 2 cf. col.1;and Figure 9—figure supplement 1D, cols. 4–5 vs. 2 cf. col. 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Strong interaction of either eIF4A or eIF4E with the Ded1-NTD is sufficient to greatly reduce the amount of Ded1 required for maximum acceleration of 48S PIC assembly on RPL41A mRNA.
source: These last results suggest that strong interaction of either eIF4A or eIF4E with the Ded1-NTD is sufficient to greatly reduce the amount of Ded1 required for maximum acceleration of 48S PIC assembly on RPL41A mRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reconstituted system data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: On CP-8.1 mRNA, eliminating either of the interactions of the Ded1-NTD with eIF4A and eIF4E conferred an increase in the Ded1 K1/2 only slightly smaller than that given by deleting the entire NTD.
source: This contrasts with our findings on CP-8.1 mRNA, where eliminating either of the interactions of the Ded1-NTD with eIF4A and eIF4E conferred an increase in the Ded1 K1/2 only slightly smaller than that given by deleting the entire NTD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the reconstituted system data for CP-8.1 mRNA in Figure 9B with that for RPL41A mRNA in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are needed simultaneously to enhance the function of the eIF4F-Ded1 complex on the more structured CP-8.1 mRNA, whereas each interaction can contribute independently and additively on the less structured RPL41A mRNA.
source: Thus, it appears that both interactions are needed simultaneously to enhance the function of the eIF4F-Ded1 complex on the more structured CP-8.1 mRNA, whereas each interaction can contribute independently and additively on the less structured RPL41A mRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the reconstituted system data for CP-8.1 mRNA in Figure 9 with that for RPL41A mRNA in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD.
source: Together, our findings indicate that the Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD, and that these interactions, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: The Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
source: Together, our findings indicate that the Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD, and that these interactions, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: In all in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD.
source: As summarized schematically in Figure 9D, in all of our in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD, and the eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple in vivo assays throughout the manuscript.

claim: The eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall for Ded1 function in vivo.
source: As summarized schematically in Figure 9D, in all of our in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD, and the eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple in vivo assays throughout the manuscript.

claim: All of the Ded1 interactions with eIF4F subunits should serve to tether Ded1 tightly to the activated eIF4F·mRNA complex and focus its helicase activity on the 5'UTR to unwind structures that impede PIC attachment or subsequent scanning.
source: Envisioning all of these interactions occurring simultaneously on an mRNA suggests that they should serve to tether Ded1 tightly to the activated eIF4F·mRNA complex and focus its helicase activity on the 5'UTR to unwind structures that impede PIC attachment or subsequent scanning (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a model proposed to explain the data, depicted in Figure 9C.

claim: The Ded1-NTD interaction with eIF4A is particularly important for enhancing Ded1 unwinding of the SL structure in CP-8.1 mRNA.
source: Consistent with previous in vitro findings that interaction with eIF4A increases Ded1 unwinding activity (Gao et al., 2016), our results here in the reconstituted system suggest that the Ded1-NTD interaction with eIF4A is particularly important for enhancing Ded1 unwinding of the SL structure in CP-8.1 mRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reconstituted system data in Figure 9A, supported by prior work.

claim: Ded1-NTD interactions with both eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, all help to assemble and stabilize the eIF4F-Ded1 complex at the 5' ends of mRNAs, which enhances initiation of nearly all mRNAs.
source: In summary, we envision that Ded1-NTD interactions with both eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, all help to assemble and stabilize the eIF4F-Ded1 complex at the 5' ends of mRNAs, which enhances initiation of nearly all mRNAs, whereas the Ded1-NTD/eIF4A interaction is additionally important to stimulate Ded1 unwinding of strong secondary structures in mRNA 5'UTRs (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a summary model proposed to explain the data, depicted in Figure 9C.
